final_content:
Napoleon III, nephew of Napoleon I, served as president of the Second French Republic (1848–1852) and later as Emperor of France (1852–1870). His key accomplishments include modernizing France’s infrastructure, promoting industrial growth, and expanding French influence in Europe through diplomacy. However, his leadership is most notably tied to the **Franco-Prussian War (1870–1871)**, which led to his capture and exile, marking the end of the Second French Empire. His policies aimed to restore imperial glory but faced criticism for authoritarianism.
